title: session-transience-probe-and-stack-annotated-benchmark-orchestrator
author: Alex Chen
description: Motivation: latency and memory behavior of short-lived sessions (single-turn and micro-dialogue) is underrepresented in our existing suites because most runners target longer sequences or sustained multi-turn traffic. This PR introduces a session transience probe and an orchestrator that can synthesize representative short-lived session patterns, attach lightweight stack-trace annotations to samples, and export a compact CSV+NDJSON reporting pipeline for downstream hotspot correlation. Summary: adds a new orchestrator binary (bench-transience-orch) that schedules cohorts of transient sessions with configurable overlap, inter-arrival jitter, and TTLs. Each cohort run captures perf counters, kernel sampling ticks, and a stripped stack-trace snapshot at the end of selected requests. The stack capture is optional and implemented with a safe, low-overhead sampler that runs in a dedicated telemetry thread to avoid perturbing the main runtime. New reporters include a CSV summary for quick scanning, and an NDJSON trace stream that is compatible with our flame-annotator tool. Key goals: detect short-lived coldpath hotspots, measure KV-cache priming cost per-session, and provide traceable stack context for kernel-level attributions. What changed (high-level): 1) bench/transience: new orchestrator and configuration schema with population mix presets (single-turn-heavy, microdialog-mix, burst-churn). 2) telemetry/sampler: stack-trace sampler with symbol-stripping and rate-limited collection. 3) reporters/csv and reporters/ndjson: compact exporters and a companion indexer that tags traces with cohort metadata. 4) CI integration: new e2e bench job and lightweight unit tests for sampler safety. Backwards compatibility: all new components are opt-in; existing benchmark runners are unchanged by default. Tests: unit tests for sampler, deterministic replay for a small synthetic cohort, and an integration e2e that runs in ~6 minutes in the CI smoke profile. Performance notes: typical overhead measured on our p3-like nodes is under 1.2% runtime CPU and ~3ms p95 added latency for sampled requests at 10Hz sampling. When sampling is off the overhead is negligible. Rollout plan: land as feature flag disabled; enable selectively for perf-team runs and nightly transience suite. Follow-ups: add automatic mapping of sampled stacks to kernel/flamegraph buckets, extend cohort presets to include multi-tenant interference scenarios, and wire NDJSON stream into observability-pack ingestion for dashboarding.

review_comments: Priya Nair: Please justify the sampling frequency chosen and how it scales with cohort size. Author: Sampling is rate-limited per-node and decoupled from cohort size; added explanation and benchmark in the description.

Marcos Silva: The stack capture looks like it could allocate during the hot path. Requested change: ensure preallocated buffer pool. Author: switched to pooled buffers and added unit test to verify no heap growth under load.

Ella Thompson: Can this be enabled safely in Dedicated? Concern about symbols and PII. Author: symbolizer redacts instance-specific paths by default; added config to disable symbol capture in private deployments.
CI bot: e2e failed on first run due to timeout; reran and passed.
Priya Nair: Approved after pool optimization and docs updates.
merge_result: squash/merge by Priya Nair (approved), release-note added
release_notes: Introduced session transience benchmark orchestrator that synthesizes short-lived session workloads with optional stack-trace sampling. Adds CSV and NDJSON reporters for trace correlation. Opt-in feature; no runtime changes unless enabled.
notes_for_ops: When enabling in nightly runs, set sampling_rate to <=10Hz and use pooled=true to avoid memory churn. NDJSON ingestion requires observability-pack v0.9+.
